page: Microsoft Azure D96pls_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dplsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated physical cores powered by the Microsoft Neoverse-N2 ARM processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The system is configured with 192.0 GB of memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is premium storage capable.

Performance benchmarks highlight exceptional multi-core capabilities, placing the server in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core execution. The dedicated physical core architecture, combined with a 128 MB L3 cache, enables high memory bandwidth, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching top-tier levels. However, single-core performance is more moderate, scoring in the average tier for single-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio represents a clear tradeoff, prioritizing raw compute density over memory capacity. This makes the D96pls_v6 highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy, memory-lean workloads. It is highly suited for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, static web serving, database operations, and medium-to-large scale LLM inference text generation, where its top-tier multi-threaded performance can be fully leveraged.
